title: Two Touches. One Header. Messi's Argentina Break England's Hearts.

scenes.voiceover: Lautaro Martínez touched the ball twice tonight. The second touch put Argentina in the World Cup final.
scenes.visualConcept: Lautaro pointing — the super-sub who needed one moment.

scenes.voiceover: For thirty minutes, England were in the final. Anthony Gordon finished Morgan Rogers' cross on fifty-five, and Atlanta went quiet.
scenes.visualConcept: Gordon in white — England's moment of belief.

scenes.voiceover: Jordan Pickford was a wall — denying Julián Álvarez twice, clawing out Nico González's header. Three saves. It still wasn't enough.
And Harry Kane? Twenty-six touches. Zero shots. In ninety minutes. One night after Spain silenced Mbappé, Argentina did the same to England's captain.
scenes.visualConcept: Kane's clean portrait — a captain erased.

scenes.voiceover: This was no chess match. Nineteen fouls in the first half alone — a street brawl in Atlanta, and Argentina kept dragging England into it.
scenes.visualConcept: Bodies flying — the acrobatic chaos of the night.

scenes.voiceover: England retreated. For the last twenty minutes they couldn't get out of their own half. And then the eighty-fifth minute happened.
Enzo Fernández — one hundred and four touches, more than anyone on the pitch — picked his moment and hammered it past Pickford from distance. One-one.
scenes.visualConcept: Enzo #24 — the engine who never stopped.

scenes.voiceover: Stoppage time. Mac Allister hits the post. The rebound falls to a thirty-nine-year-old Lionel Messi... and time stops.
scenes.visualConcept: Messi glancing over his shoulder — the calm before.

scenes.voiceover: The cross is perfect. Lautaro Martínez rises. Header. Two-one. His second touch of the entire game wins it.
scenes.visualConcept: Messi and Lautaro embracing — the goal in one image.

scenes.voiceover: Messi's night at thirty-nine: ninety-four touches. Twelve duels won. Both assists. He didn't score — he just decided the game anyway.
scenes.visualConcept: Messi sitting on the turf — the weary king.

scenes.voiceover: Eleven of Argentina's goals at this World Cup have come after the seventy-fifth minute. Eleven. They don't chase games. They hunt them.
scenes.visualConcept: Lautaro in full sprint — the late-game predator.

scenes.voiceover: So it's Spain versus Argentina. The team that never concedes... against the team that never dies. Messi's last World Cup dance — Sunday.
scenes.visualConcept: The World Cup trophy — the prize.

scenes.voiceover: Does Messi finally get his second star — or does Spain's machine shut him down too? Comment your pick, and follow — we'll be live for the final.
